_comment: Bounded completion-decision cases for #861 criteria 2 and 3.
`work` is an honest account of what the implementation did, written the way a
worker would describe it. The EXPECTED disposition is deliberately not in the
prompt - it lives only in `expect_closes` and `probes`, which are used to score
the run afterwards. A prompt that names the answer measures nothing.
The issue handed to the model is not written here: it is GENERATED by the real
converter from spec-v1.md + tasks.md, then carries a recorded revision naming
ONE VARIABLE PER CASE. c2 is the control and every other case is c2 with exactly
one thing removed, so a differing disposition is attributable to that one thing.
The first run of these cases did NOT have this property: the control omitted
evidence for R1, a requirement the generated context block declares, and the
model correctly refused to close it. That was a defect in the fixture, not in
the model, and it is why every case now carries R1 evidence.

cases.name: c1-revision-preserved-item-unmet

probes.criterion: 2 and 3 together - the case the wave asked for
probes.varies_from_control: cancellation is not implemented; everything else is identical
probes.must_reach_report: the cancel item, named as not delivered
probes.hazard: handling the revision well and calling the whole issue complete

cases.work: The 200ms target was revised during implementation and the reviewer agreed in the issue thread (see the recorded Acceptance-revision line): a 50k-row export cannot render inside 200ms on the supported hardware, so the export now streams in chunks and the page stays interactive throughout instead. The revised behaviour is covered by tests/test_exports.py::test_page_stays_interactive_during_50k_export, which drives a 50k-row export and asserts the page handles input at every chunk boundary; it passes. Exports run off the request thread on a worker: tests/test_exports.py::test_export_does_not_hold_a_request_thread asserts the request returns before the export finishes and the worker completes it; it passes. Cancellation was not implemented. There is no cancel control on the exports page and nothing in the diff touches it. make lint and make test are green - 63 tests pass.

cases.name: c2-control-every-item-met

probes.criterion: positive control for c1 and c3
probes.must_reach_report: both acceptance items and both declared requirements, demonstrated
probes.hazard: a run that answers Refs to everything scores perfectly on c1 and c3 alone

cases.work: The 200ms target was revised during implementation and the reviewer agreed in the issue thread (see the recorded Acceptance-revision line): a 50k-row export cannot render inside 200ms on the supported hardware, so the export now streams in chunks and the page stays interactive throughout instead. The revised behaviour is covered by tests/test_exports.py::test_page_stays_interactive_during_50k_export, which drives a 50k-row export and asserts the page handles input at every chunk boundary; it passes. Exports run off the request thread on a worker: tests/test_exports.py::test_export_does_not_hold_a_request_thread asserts the request returns before the export finishes and the worker completes it; it passes. Cancellation is implemented: the exports page has a Cancel control, and tests/test_exports.py::test_cancel_stops_writing_and_releases_the_handle asserts the writer stops and the file handle is released; it passes. make lint and make test are green - 65 tests pass.

cases.name: c3-revision-recorded-without-evidence

probes.criterion: 3 - a revision record is not delivery evidence
probes.varies_from_control: nothing exercises the revised streaming behaviour; everything else is identical
probes.must_reach_report: that no test exercises the revised behaviour
probes.hazard: reading the recorded agreement as though it were the evidence

cases.work: The 200ms target was revised during implementation and the reviewer agreed in the issue thread (see the recorded Acceptance-revision line): a 50k-row export cannot render inside 200ms on the supported hardware, so the export now streams in chunks instead. No test exercises the streaming behaviour. The only performance test in the suite is tests/test_exports.py::test_export_is_not_slow, written for the old target, which still passes because it asserts the export finishes within 30 seconds. Exports run off the request thread on a worker: tests/test_exports.py::test_export_does_not_hold_a_request_thread asserts the request returns before the export finishes and the worker completes it; it passes. Cancellation is implemented: the exports page has a Cancel control, and tests/test_exports.py::test_cancel_stops_writing_and_releases_the_handle asserts the writer stops and the file handle is released; it passes. make lint and make test are green - 64 tests pass.
